title: InferOps V1 decision ownership and sign-off authority
description: Who is accountable for each accepted V1 architectural decision, who may accept or amend one, who signs off that a published claim matches its evidence, and who approves a V1 release. It is committed as data so that an unassigned owner is a test failure rather than a sentence nobody re-reads. It records accountability and nothing else: no entry here raises a certification level, changes an evidence class, or turns a documented, mock, synthetic, or estimated result into a real-runtime one.

roles.name: The repository maintainer role
roles.heldBy: Anyone able to merge a pull request into `main` in this repository.
roles.conferredBy: Write access to this repository, which the repository's own settings decide and no document here can grant.
roles.whyNotAPerson: A person named in a record goes stale the day they stop merging, and a record that names a person who no longer acts is worse than one that names the role that still does. The role is the long-lived unit; who holds it is repository state, not published prose.

authorities.name: Decision ownership
authorities.question: Who is accountable for an accepted architectural decision continuing to describe the system?
authorities.exercisedBy: Carrying the record: amending it when the implementation moves, or superseding it when the decision no longer holds.
doesNotEstablish: that the owner independently re-derived the evidence the record cites
that the record's claims were reviewed by anyone outside this repository
that anything the record describes was observed running

authorities.name: Acceptance and amendment authority
authorities.question: Who may accept, amend, or supersede a V1 architectural decision?
authorities.exercisedBy: Approving and merging the pull request that carries the record or the amendment. The merge is the act; there is no separate approval artifact.
doesNotEstablish: that the accepted decision is supported by evidence it does not cite
that a status may be raised without the evidence the status requires
that acceptance substitutes for the per-decision table a partial record has to carry

authorities.name: Claim and evidence sign-off
authorities.question: Who signs that a published claim's status matches the evidence the register binds to it?
authorities.exercisedBy: Merging the change that sets or moves a claim's status in the claim and evidence register, having read the record the row cites.
doesNotEstablish: that the claim was reviewed by an outside party
that the evidence behind the claim changed class because it was signed
that a certification level moved; a level is reached by a record, never by an approval

authorities.name: Release approval
authorities.question: Who approves a V1 release candidate, as far as architecture and governance are concerned?
authorities.exercisedBy: Approving the exact candidate commit named in the release checklist, after the gates that checklist requires have passed.
doesNotEstablish: that the released state was assessed by anyone outside this repository
that a version number is evidence of runtime, performance, or production fitness
that a gate which did not run may be reported as passed

ownershipBases.assigned-retrospectively: The record was accepted before this ownership model existed. The role takes accountability for the record going forward. Nobody re-read the historical evidence as part of the assignment, and the assignment is not a review of it.
ownershipBases.assigned-at-acceptance: The record was accepted under this ownership model, and the owner was named when it was accepted.

transferRules: The role is the owner; a change of holder transfers nothing, because no record names a holder. A new maintainer acquires every decision this file assigns to the role on the day they can merge, and loses it on the day they cannot.

While the role has one holder, a record is accepted by that holder and the merge is the whole act. This is stated rather than implied, because a single-holder approval is the weakest form of the four authorities and a reader is entitled to know which one they are looking at.

When the role has more than one holder, the maintainer who accepts or amends a record must not be its author. The review requirement in CONTRIBUTING already implies a second reader; this makes it explicit for a decision record, which is the class of change least likely to fail a test when it is wrong.

A future split of the four authorities across different roles is an amendment to this file and the record behind it, not a new convention adopted in passing. Nothing here reserves the authorities to one role permanently; it records that today they are held by one because there is one.
limits: Sign-off under this model is internal. No outside party has reviewed a decision, a claim, or a release candidate in this repository, and merging a change is not an external review.

Assigning an owner to a record accepted before this model existed does not mean the owner re-derived that record's evidence. Every such entry carries the `assigned-retrospectively` basis for exactly that reason.

No authority here changes what a result may be used to claim. Certification levels are reached by records, evidence classes are set by the layer that produced the result, and an approval moves neither.

No public roster names who holds the maintainer role. That is deliberate under this model rather than pending: the role is the published unit. A reader who needs to know who merged a change reads the commit history, which is the only place this repository answers that.
This file records authority over decisions, claims, and releases. It confers no authority over anything in a running system, because nothing in this repository administers one.
